title: The part window title row shows Active or Inactive beside the close X
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Have an active part, part A, and an inactive part, part B, at the test location.
  • Start on the Inventory page (Parts in the top bar, then Inventory in the left menu), on the Active tab.
custom_steps:
1. Click New Inventory Part.
  2. Click the X at the right end of the title row.
  3. Type part A's part number in the Search box.
  4. Click the part A row.
  5. Click the X at the right end of the title row.
  6. Click the Inactive tab.
  7. Type part B's part number in the Search box.
  8. Click the part B row.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • The window is titled "New Inventory Part". A thin line runs under the title row, with the close X at its right end.
  • No status pill shows in the title row.

Step 2:

  • The window closes.

Step 3:

  • Part A is listed.

Step 4:

  • The window is titled "Edit Inventory Part", with a thin line under the title row and a green pill reading "Active" beside the close X.

Step 5:

  • The window closes.

Step 6:

  • The Inactive tab is selected.

Step 7:

  • Part B is listed.

Step 8:

  • The title row shows a grey pill reading "Inactive" beside the close X.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Parts Lifecycle Update", Confluence 829227015, version 33 (23 Oct 2026, owner Chris Ward), read 27 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-10647, story SV-10826 (Story 13, The Part Dialog), story SV-10822 (Story 9, Inactive Parts Cannot Be Added to New Work)

  • S13-R1: “The dialog is titled "New Inventory Part" when creating a part and "Edit Inventory Part" when editing one.”
  • S13-R2: “The title row has a thin line under it, and the close X at its right end.”
  • S13-R3: “When editing, the title row shows the part's saved status as a pill beside the close X: "Active" in green, or "Inactive" in grey.”
  • S9-R14: “The part dialog of an inactive part shows the grey "Inactive" badge in its title row (S13-R3).”
